sections.title: Visual Pitch (§30M)
sections.md:
### Visual plan

The strongest picture for every line, picked from three (hooks from five). Scores out of 12: stop · line · feel · specific · fresh · makeable.

### Act 1 — the years of foundations: her honest bare face, the shelf growing, and every bottle caking in her lines

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B01 | And for years I felt like my own face | from behind her shoulder she runs her eyes along forty unlabelled bottles on her shelf, one hand on the dresser | WORLD | 12/12 | LITERAL: her face in close-up, looking down (7) · SYMBOL: a calendar of years (4) |
| B02 | had quietly turned on me. | over her shoulder into a round hand mirror: her bare tired face looking back at her | REACTION | 12/12 | LITERAL: her face turning away from the lens (7) · CONTRAST: an old photo of her younger face beside the mirror (10) |
| B03 | The dull, tired skin. | in the mirror glass, her bare cheek and eye: dull, sallow, matte skin, one slow blink | DETAIL | 12/12 | LITERAL: a macro of skin texture alone (8) · STAKES: her sighing at the mirror (8) |
| B04 | The deep lines. | side-on macro: her deep crow's feet hold their shadows as her eyes narrow, then relax | DETAIL | 12/12 | LITERAL: her forehead lines front-on (8) · SYMBOL: cracked dry earth (6) |
| B05 | The dark circles that made me look worn out | from just below, her eyes lift from the mirror to the lens, the dark circles under both eyes plain in the window light | STAKES | 12/12 | LITERAL: a macro of one dark circle (8) · REACTION: her rubbing her eyes (7) |
| B06 | I bought the next foundation, then the next, | square on the shelf, her hand sets one more unlabelled bottle at the end of a row, then a second beside it | PROOF | 11/12 | WORLD: a pile of shopping bags on the floor (7) · LITERAL: one bottle on a counter (6) |
| B07 | then the two hundred dollar one, | from above, her hands lift a heavy faceted glass bottle with a gold cap out of white tissue in a cream box | DETAIL | 12/12 | STAKES: a receipt with a big total (7) · LITERAL: the bottle on the shelf (6) |
| B08 | always sure the next one would finally fix it. | at the hand mirror she dots the new foundation on her cheek with one fingertip and looks, hopeful | REACTION | 12/12 | SYMBOL: her fingers crossed (6) · LITERAL: the new bottle's pump pressed (6) |
| B09 ★ hero | It sat on top, sank into my lines, | side-on macro: a flat beige foundation sits cakey on her skin and has settled into every crow's foot, each crease a darker line of product | STAKES | 12/12 | CONTRAST: half her cheek bare, half caked (9) · LITERAL: foundation on a fingertip (6) |
| B10 | oxidized, and left me looking more tired than my bare face. | over her shoulder into the hand mirror: her caked face gone patchy and orange along the jaw against a paler neck; she lowers the mirror | STAKES | 12/12 | DETAIL: a macro of the orange line at the jaw (10) · LITERAL: her frowning (6) |

### Act 2 — the paint wall: a factory colour rolled on sits as a coat and sinks into the cracks — exactly as foundation does in her lines

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B11 ★ hero | Think of your skin like a wall | low and wide: she steps beside the bare warm plaster wall, bottle in one hand, and lays her other palm flat on it | SYMBOL | 12/12 | LITERAL: a close-up of a plaster wall (7) · WORLD: a hardware store paint aisle (7) |
| B12 | Every foundation you have ever bought | at the wall she raises the beige foundation bottle to shoulder height like an exhibit, eyes on the lens | PRODUCT | 11/12 | WORLD: her shelf of forty bottles again (7) · LITERAL: a bottle on a white table (6) |
| B13 | works exactly like a pre-mixed can of paint from a factory, | top-down: the open can of flat pinkish-beige paint, and her hand sets the beige foundation bottle right beside it — the same colour | CONTRAST | 11/12 | WORLD: a paint factory line filling cans (8) · LITERAL: a closed paint can (6) |
| B14 | You bring it home, put it on, | from behind her shoulder she rolls the beige paint up the bare wall in one long slow stroke | LITERAL | 11/12 | DETAIL: the roller's nap pressing into the wall (9) · WORLD: carrying the can in from the car (7) |
| B15 | and it is never quite your color. | low and square: she steps back and tilts her head at the flat pinkish stripe, plainly wrong against the warm plaster | CONTRAST | 12/12 | DETAIL: the stripe's colour next to the bare wall, close (9) · REACTION: her wince (7) |
| B16 | It sits there as an obvious coat. | macro across the stripe's edge: a flat ridge of beige sitting on top of the plaster with a hard edge | DETAIL | 11/12 | CONTRAST: the coated and bare wall side by side (8) · LITERAL: a wet paint sign (4) |
| B17 | And on a wall with any texture or fine cracks, | square macro: the beige coat slides over fine hairline cracks and sinks in, each crack turning to a darker line | MECHANISM | 12/12 | LITERAL: the bare cracks alone (8) · DETAIL: a fingertip tracing one crack (9) |
| B18 | like skin over fifty, it sinks straight into them and makes them worse. | the same square macro on her cheek: beige foundation sinks into her fine lines in the same pattern as the wall's cracks | CONTRAST | 12/12 | STAKES: her whole caked face in the mirror again (8) · LITERAL: a macro of fine lines, bare (7) |

### Act 3 — the opposite: no shade at all — white that becomes her shade on her face, in one unbroken shot

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B19 | This does the opposite. It does not come in a shade. | at the wall she sets the beige bottle down by the paint can and holds up the closed violet stick beside her face, wordmark to the lens | PRODUCT | 11/12 | CONTRAST: the paint can and the stick side by side on the drop cloth (10) · LITERAL: the stick on a white table (6) |
| B20 | It comes out pure white. I know what you are thinking. Stay with me. | a little low: she draws the cap off and turns the white balm to the lens, the corner of her mouth lifting, knowing | PRODUCT | 12/12 | DETAIL: a macro of the white crest (9) · REACTION: her eyebrow raised to the lens (8) |
| B21 ★ hero | It reads the warmth of your own skin and becomes your exact shade, right there on your face. No shade to pick. No wrong match. It adapts as it goes on. | one unbroken side-on macro of her bare cheek: a white stripe goes on, the brush circles through it — white ahead of the crown, her own shade behind — until the cheek is one even tone, every line still there | PROOF | 11/12 | CONTRAST: white stripe, then the blended cheek, cut together (8) · LITERAL: the stick turning on a table (5) |

### Act 4 — the result on the same face: even, matched, every line still hers — and the factory bottle goes back on the shelf

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B22 ★ hero | It covers the lines, the dark circles, the tired. | she turns her finished face slowly from profile to the lens in the window light: even tone, the circles gone, every line still there | PROOF | 12/12 | CONTRAST: her bare face cut to her finished face (9) · LITERAL: a macro of her finished under-eye (8) |
| B23 | My skin, on its best day. Finally the right match, | she holds the beige bottle up beside her finished cheek: the flat factory beige next to her even, matched skin | CONTRAST | 12/12 | PROOF: a macro of her cheek, pores and lines, the tone even (9) · REACTION: her looking at her reflection, pleased (8) |
| B24 | instead of a guess from a factory. | from above her shoulder she sets the beige bottle back on the shelf among the forty others and lets go | SYMBOL | 12/12 | PRODUCT: the stick set down in front of the shelf (7) · LITERAL: a factory conveyor of bottles (5) |

### Act 5 — the deal on her dresser, then the stick alone in soft light

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B25 | two Foundation Sticks for almost the price of one, | from above the dresser her hand sets a second stick upright beside the first, both wordmarks to the lens | PRODUCT | 11/12 | CONTRAST: one stick, then two (8) · LITERAL: two sticks on a white background (7) |
| B26 | plus a free primer, a mystery gift, | level with the dresser her hand sets the primer and then the small gift box beside the two sticks, the box lid ajar on a fold of white tissue | DETAIL | 11/12 | PRODUCT: level with the dresser her hand sets the primer and then the small gift box beside the two sticks (9) · LITERAL: the primer alone (6) |
| B27 ★ hero | Stop paying for a color that was never yours. | the closed violet stick stands on the white dresser and turns a quarter turn in soft window light, the wordmark coming round, the shelf of bottles soft behind | PRODUCT | 12/12 | CONTRAST: the stick in front, forty bottles behind it in focus (10) · LITERAL: a price tag (5) |
